Resampling frequencies of the skeleton and of each orientation

Source: R/bootstrap.R
mc_cpdag_stability.Rd

Repeats the constraint-based discovery of mc_graph_pipeline over resamples and records, for every pair of responses, how often the pair came out absent, undirected, or directed each way. An orientation that the data barely support shows up here as a pair whose two directions split the frequency, which a single run cannot reveal.

Usage

mc_cpdag_stability(
  fit,
  B = 100L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  orient_method = c("pc", "hc", "tabu"),
  orient_rule = c("standard", "conservative", "majority"),
  required = NULL,
  forbidden = NULL,
  refit = c("residual", "full"),
  cluster = NULL,
  max_ord = NULL,
  df_residual = NULL,
  workers = 1L
)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_cpdag_stability'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph".

B

number of resamples, an integer of at least two; default 100.

alpha

significance level of the second-order separation test.

orient_method

"pc" (native, default), "hc" or "tabu" (bnlearn). When bnlearn is not installed, the last two fall back on "pc" with a warning, and the result records it in orientation_fallback.

orient_rule

rule for the unshielded triples of the native route: "standard" (default), "conservative" or "majority". It has no effect when orient_method is a score-based route.

required, forbidden

optional background knowledge, as two-column matrices of arcs \((from, to)\) given either by response name or by index. An arc in required must be present with that direction, an arc in forbidden must not. They are imposed before propagation, and Meek's fourth rule, idle without them, carries their consequences through the rest of the graph. Available on the native route only.

refit

"residual" (default) or "full", as above; "full" corresponds to stage = "both" of mc_graph_bootstrap.

cluster

optional vector with one identifier per row, with no missing values and at least two distinct values; whole clusters are resampled. Required with refit = "full" when the within-response structure is not the identity, as in mc_graph_bootstrap.

max_ord

maximum conditioning order; NULL uses \(R - 2\).

df_residual

optional residual degrees of freedom \(\nu_e\): NULL (default) uses the raw-sample contract based on \(n\); a number or the result of mc_residual_df is used as given; "auto" computes it with mc_residual_df and refuses a fit for which it is not exact.

workers

number of parallel workers, default 1. The resamples are drawn in the parent, so a given seed yields the same ones at any worker count.

x

an object of class "mcg_cpdag_stability".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_cpdag_stability": a list with states, a data frame with one row per pair of responses (i, j, response1, response2) and the frequencies of the four states (absent, undirected, i_to_j, j_to_i); the symmetric matrix edge_prob of skeleton frequencies, one minus absent; consensus, the 0/1 adjacency matrix that gives each pair its most frequent state, the first in the order above on a tie (an entry [i, j] equal to one alone reads \(i\to j\), with [j, i] also one the edge is undirected); being formed pair by pair, it need not be the CPDAG of a DAG; valid_prob, the proportion of valid resamples whose output passed the validity gates of mc_graph_pipeline; mean_ambiguous, the average number of ambiguous triples per valid resample; the counts B, B_valid and B_failed; B_incomplete, the number of valid resamples in which the skeleton search skipped a test that could not be formed, as in mc_pc_skeleton, reported in one warning when it is not zero; the data frame failures (replicate, error); and the settings refit, alpha, orient_method, orient_rule, clustered (logical) and response_names. The print method shows the settings, the counts and the table of frequencies, and returns its argument invisibly.

What each resample is

With refit = "residual" the resample is drawn from the stored Pearson residuals and the first stage is held fixed, so the frequencies describe the discovery step alone. With refit = "full" rows of the data are resampled and both stages are refitted, so they carry the variability of the whole procedure. Units are drawn with replacement, keeping the sample size, which is the bootstrap convention (Efron, 1979); mc_graph_stability instead uses half-samples, the convention of the stability-selection literature (Meinshausen and Buhlmann, 2010). With \(B_v\) valid resamples, the frequency of a state is the proportion of valid resamples in which the pair is in it, so the four frequencies of a pair sum to one; a resample whose refit or pipeline raises an error is dropped and recorded in failures, and at least one valid resample is required.

What the frequencies estimate

Each frequency estimates, by resampling, the probability that the discovery procedure, at the given alpha and orientation rule, returns that state for the pair in a sample of the same size. It measures the stability of the output of the procedure. It is not the probability that the edge or the orientation belongs to the structure that generated the data, and it carries no control of an error rate.

References

Efron, B. (1979). Bootstrap methods: another look at the jackknife. The Annals of Statistics 7(1), 1–26. doi:10.1214/aos/1176344552

Meinshausen, N. and Buhlmann, P. (2010). Stability selection. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B 72(4), 417–473. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2010.00740.x

See also

mc_graph_pipeline for a single run and mc_graph_bootstrap for the bootstrap of the graph parameters.

Other resampling: mc_graph_bootstrap()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 400; x <- rnorm(n)
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7 * z1 + 0.7 * z2 + rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = z1, y2 = z2, y3 = z3, x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_cpdag_stability(f, B = 50)
#> Structure frequencies (pc, standard rule, alpha = 0.05, B = 50)
#> Resamples: residuals resampled, first stage held fixed | valid: 50 | failed: 0
#> Outputs passing the validity gates: 100%
#> 
#>   response1 response2 absent undirected i_to_j j_to_i
#> 1        y1        y2   0.94       0.06   0.00      0
#> 2        y1        y3   0.00       0.06   0.94      0
#> 3        y2        y3   0.00       0.06   0.94      0
# }
